11417.why: Leutze's boat is overloaded, the river is full of ice, and every person in it is pulling in the same direction.

10481.why: Church packed a whole continent into one view, from the snow on the peak to the moss on the rocks at your feet.

10497.why: Cole's Oxbow is a storm leaving on one side and sun arriving on the other, with the painter alone in between.

12127.why: Sargent's Madame X turns her face away and lets you look. Composed on the outside, and a scandal underneath.

10159.why: Bingham's fur traders drift downriver through pink morning haze, with a cat in the bow and nowhere to hurry to.

10154.why: Bierstadt's mountains are bigger than anything you have ever seen, and the light is just breaking over them.

11311.why: Kensett's Lake George is a still morning with nothing moving. The quietest picture in the wing.

11050.why: Heade painted the minute before a storm: black sky, flat water, and one man on the shore who has not moved yet.

11145.why: Homer's veteran has put down his rifle and picked up a scythe. Hot sun, tall wheat, and a lot to think about.

10819.why: Eakins put his friend alone on a glassy river in clear autumn light, resting between strokes.

11122.why: Homer's sailor is adrift with sharks circling and a waterspout coming, and he is not looking at either.

10464.why: Chase painted a bright day at the beach with red umbrellas and children digging in the sand.

10813.why: Eakins painted his father watching two old friends play chess in a dark, comfortable room.

10554.why: Copley's rescue is one second from going wrong, and nine people are reaching at once.

16584.why: Stuart left this portrait of Washington unfinished on purpose, and kept it to copy for the rest of his life.

24671.why: Henry II's parade armor is covered in gold and silver figures. It was never meant for a fight, only for being seen.

23944.why: Ferdinand I rode into the Equestrian Court in this. It still has the feel of a parade.

23939.why: George Clifford had this blued and gilded armor made for tilting in front of the Queen. Confidence in steel.

22860.why: A helmet shaped like a roaring gilt lion. Somebody wanted to be noticed, and five hundred years later they still are.

22634.why: Negroli hammered a mermaid and a Medusa out of one sheet of steel. Close up, the detail stops time.

22506.why: A fourteenth-century samurai armor of silk cord and lacquered scales, made for a man who founded a dynasty.

22521.why: Dark lacquer, blue silk and a quiet, upright posture. This armor is about discipline, not display.

24693.why: Girolamo da Treviso painted a whole battle onto a parade shield, gold on dark ground, horses everywhere.

23216.why: A frog-mouth helm for the joust, built for the roar of a crowd and the moment two riders meet.

24937.why: A tiny gilded armor made for a five-year-old prince. Equal parts serious and sweet.

24931.why: Fancy-dress armor for a costume ball in 1790, made to look like a Roman hero. Pure theater.

27792.why: Black steel and gilt for a king of Portugal. Armor from the last century anyone wore it to war.

23358.why: Lochner made this horse armor for a duke who liked to be looked at. The whole court rides in a line.
